title: Model advertisement schema for version pinning and performance profile broadcast
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood needs a stable, machine-readable way to 'advertise' a model's capabilities and performance profile as part of onboarding and runtime selection. Current model manifests are fragmented across internal endpoints and lack a concise publishable schema that (a) surfaces feature gates, context and token limits, perf estimates, and quantization/variant compatibility, and (b) explicitly supports operator-driven version pinning for Dedicated/Private customers.

Goals:
- Define a single advertisement schema (JSON) used by onboarding pipelines and the model catalog API to broadcast capabilities and deterministic performance estimates.
- Ensure fields support runtime routing and automated fallback (e.g., version affinity, model_variant_id, compatible_pin_targets).
- Backwards-compatibly expose this via a new API path so older clients are unaffected while we migrate Console & SDKs.
- Provide clear semantics for pinning: how a customer 'pins' to a version and how the runtime resolves conflicts and fallbacks.

Key schema primitives (proposed):
- model_id: stable catalog id
- model_variant_id: GPU/quantization variant tag (e.g., v1-int8, v1-fp16)
- digest: sha256 of served artifact
- release_channel: [stable|beta|experimental]
- pinned_versions: list of version identifiers allowed for customer pinning (for Dedicated/Private)
- version_affinity: priority-ordered list (preferred -> fallback)
- features: list of capability strings (tool-calling, streaming, structured_output, embeddings, reranking)
- limits: {context_tokens, request_token_limit, concurrency_limit} (serialized as flat fields context_tokens, request_token_limit, concurrency_limit)
- perf_profile: list of perf rows (seq_length, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec) represented as strings e.g. "seq:128|p95:45ms|tps:120" to avoid nested objects in documents
- memory_estimate_mb: single numeric string
- compatibility_tags: list (cpu-only, cuda-11, triton-optimized)
- quant_profiles: list (quant-int8, quant-ptq, quant-llm.int4)
- constraints: freeform string for special caveats (e.g., "KV-cache not persisted across warm pools")
- publish_time / schema_version: timestamps and version strings

API surface & compatibility:
- New read endpoint: GET /v2/model-advertisements/{model_id} returns the advertised schema. This keeps existing /v1/manifests stable.
- Onboarding pipeline writes to the advertisement store as final step; the model-catalog service publishes notifications (model.advertisement.published).
- Runtime gateway uses advertisement.schema_version and release_channel to decide routing and whether to apply a translation fallback for older clients.
- Pinning semantics: customers may create a pin that references model_id + allowed variant list. The runtime resolves pins by checking advertised pinned_versions and version_affinity; if a requested pinned version is unavailable, runtime consults affinity list and then global fallback chain. Pins are treated as a hard constraint for Dedicated; for Hosted we allow "soft pins" that prefer but don't block fallback unless customer sets strict_pin=true (Console toggle).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (hosted read-only): implement GET endpoint and onboarding writer; Surface in Console as read-only model card. Deploy runtime gateway translation layer that understands new advertisement fields. (2 weeks)
- Phase 2 (SDK & Console): SDKs switch to prefer advertisement endpoint when available; Console adds pin UI upstream that writes pin requests to pins service which validates against advertised pinned_versions. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (Dedicated/Private): add validation in Dedicated control plane to reject pins that reference incompatible variants; include an offline importer for legacy manifests. (3 weeks)

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Events: model.advertisement.published, model.advertisement.changed, model.pin.attempt, model.pin.conflict, model.profile.mismatch_detected.
- Success metrics: reduce routing fallback conflicts by 80% for newly onboarded models; <1% pin-resolution errors post-rollout.

Migration & Backwards compatibility notes:
- We will not change the existing manifest endpoint. All onboarding writers will write both manifest and advertisement to avoid race conditions.
- Gateway will support both shapes for 3 months; after that we will deprecate reading non-advertisement fields from runtime routing paths.
- Console will show a compatibility warning for models missing perf_profile rows or limits.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Perf profile shape: we chose a string-serialized row to keep ticket JSON flat; runtime and Console will parse these into structured objects. This avoids nested storage schema changes in the short term but requires parsing logic in two places.
- How strictly should Dedicated enforce pinned_versions vs runtime fallback? Proposal: Dedicated default = strict; Hosted default = permissive.
- Do we need an additional signature (KMS-signed digest) to trust published advertisements? Current plan: add digest and audit log; defer KMS signing to a follow-up security task.

Deliverables:
- JSON schema doc in Confluence + OpenAPI spec for GET /v2/model-advertisements/{id}
- Runtime translation layer and catalog writer PRs
- Console UI updates for pin creation + model card
- Tests: unit for parsing perf rows, integration test for pin conflict resolution, e2e routing test verifying fallback chain
